spans.s:
Stukā denotes a ‘tuft’ of hair or wool in the Rigveda and later.
Foot notes ix. 97, 17.
kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxv. 6; Av. vii. 74, 2; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iii. 2, 1, 13, etc.

Stuti in the Rigveda and later denotes a ‘song of praise.’
Foot notes i. 84, 2; vi. 34, 1; x. 31, 5.
Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, vii. 5, 2, 39
Stupa means ‘tuft of hair’ in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (ii. 2; xxv. 2) and the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa (i. 3, 3, 5; iii. 5, 3, 4). See stukā.

Stūpa in the Rigveda and later denotes the ‘top-knot’ of hair as designating the upper part of the head.
Foot notes vii. 2, 1. Cf. i. 24, 7.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, iii. 3, 6, 5; pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xiii. 4, 4.
